findings.title: Working-hours check uses slot start twice, ignoring event length
findings.body: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` computes `end` from the slot *start* instead of `slotEndTime`. As a result the check `end > workingHour.endTime` can never detect a slot whose end extends past the end of working hours, so bookings that overrun the organizer's availability are still offered. It should be derived from `slotEndTime`.

findings.title: Working-hours filter rejects slot if any single working-hours entry doesn't contain it
findings.body: The `workingHours.find(...)` predicate returns true for the first entry that does not contain the slot (different day or different time block), and any truthy result makes the function return `false` (unavailable). With multiple availability rows (e.g. split hours 9-12 and 14-18, or several day groups) virtually every slot matches some non-containing entry and is wrongly marked unavailable. The logic must be inverted: the slot is unavailable only if *no* working-hours entry contains it.

findings.title: Dayjs objects compared with === (always false)
findings.body: `if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes"))` compares two distinct Dayjs object references, which is never true. The intended "full-day unavailable override (start == end)" branch is therefore dead code, so zero-length overrides marking a day unavailable are not handled as designed; use `.isSame()`.

findings.title: Override day comparison mixes server-local and UTC formatting
findings.body: `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD")` formats in the server's local timezone while `slotStartTime.format(...)` is UTC (`time.utc()`). On any server not running in UTC the day strings can differ, so overrides are matched to the wrong day (or not matched), making slots wrongly available/unavailable depending on deployment timezone. Both sides should be computed in the same, explicit timezone.

findings.title: Override timeZone may be undefined, silently falling back to server local time
findings.body: `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone)` is called with `override.timeZone` typed as optional (`TimeRange.timeZone?: string`). When undefined, dayjs falls back to the server's local zone, producing an incorrect `organizerUtcOffset` and therefore shifting date-override slots by an arbitrary amount. Guard with a required timezone or an explicit UTC default.

findings.title: Override start/end converted to minutes-of-day loses day boundary crossings
findings.body: `startTime`/`endTime` are computed as `hour()*60 + minute()` after applying the invitee/organizer offset. If the offset pushes the override past midnight (common for large timezone differences) the resulting minute-of-day wraps, so endTime can become smaller than startTime (or 0 for midnight) and the override yields no slots or a bogus range. The conversion needs to account for day overflow (e.g. add 1440 when the date shifts).

findings.title: New timezone override assertion can pass with missing slots
findings.body: The `toHaveTimeSlots` matcher only iterates the *actual* slots with `.every` and never compares array lengths, so a result containing a subset (or zero) of the expected slots for that date passes. The newly added `+6:00` timezone assertion therefore does not actually guarantee the date-override timezone fix; add a length/exact-array comparison.
